findings.where: src\manifest.json l.20 (residual-search hypothesis); rendered blake3-r2\experiments\manifest.json l.20
findings.what: "batch_stage_2_entered = 1 for at most about 0.109375 of the seeds" presents a bound on an expectation as a bound on a count of 256 seeds. The expected count is about 26.7 with standard deviation 4.9, so more than 28 of 256 has probability about 0.36 and more than 32 (the H3 budget share of one eighth) about 0.12. My two seed sets gave 30 and 32 of 256 (review\judge_time.out); the local intake gave 22. With organizer seeds other than the local ones, the organizer-run report can contradict a declared prediction, and the experiments role must discuss H3.
findings.fix: Replace with: "batch_stage_2_entered = 1 for a share of about 0.104 of the seeds on average if trials satisfy rule A with probability 2^-6 (at most 7 * 2^-6 = 0.109375): about 27 of 256 seeds with a standard deviation of about 5, so the count of one run can lie above one eighth of the seeds by chance and is no test of H3." Rebuild and revalidate (hashes change).

findings.what: "The program never imports or calls an implementation of BLAKE3" is contradicted two lines later and by the code: residual-search calls batch_check -> reference -> compress2, a complete 2-round compression of the trial's messages. findings.where: proof.md l.1251-1259 and l.1929-1933 ("nothing is known about whether they satisfy rule A"); note l.228-235
findings.what: An out-of-sample figure for rule A exists and is not stated. The rule was read from the 30 betas with k at most 13: 27 of 242 outcomes have a violating solution, carrying 10,606 of 29,862,848 (0.036%). On the nine betas added later (all k = 14; 115,074) it is 13 of 45 outcomes carrying 1,434 (1.25%), a share 35 times larger; six of those nine betas are dropped in full (review\judge_time.out). The bound is not affected, but a judge can compute this from the two tables.
findings.fix: Add both figures to Section 10 (rule A paragraph and Limits) and the note, with one sentence: betas the rule was not read from comply less, and betas with k above 14, which are not counted, may be rejected more often.

findings.what: Solver results are written as facts: "every outcome ... for which a solution that violates rule A exists" is left out, and "every solution of these outcomes satisfies rule A". Both hold only if the 247 "no solution" answers are right. The abstract (l.44-45) and claim.json word it correctly.
findings.fix: Write "for which the solver found a solution that violates rule A" and "if these answers are right, every solution of these outcomes satisfies rule A".

findings.where: proof.md l.1229-1231, l.1924-1928; claim.json l.33 (H1 limitations, "one SAT solver's uncertified answers"); note l.210-211, l.505-507
findings.what: "One solver, one run" can be improved. I repeated all 287 questions with a CNF written separately from proof 6.2 (unknown Y14 instead of h1; the four output differences of the residual as conditions) and two other solvers. cadical (18 s) and cryptominisat5 (23 s) both give 247 without and 40 with a violating solution, the same answer as kissat for every outcome; all 287 base systems are satisfiable and every model checks in plain arithmetic (review\judge_sat.py, judge_sat_*.out). findings.where: claim.json l.49-51 (H3 extrapolation, limitations: "four runs cannot exclude seed words for which it has"); proof.md l.837-847, l.2004-2009
findings.what: H3 rests on four sets of seed words in a layout with two stated differences. A CPU check removes both differences and widens the base (review\judge_h3.py, Windows Python with numpy, 60 s, 5 processes): 8,192 sets of seed words in the layout of 6.4 (X1 = X10 = 0, X12 < 2^8, X13 < 2^16), 2^15 sampled batches each, 1,878,904,437 lanes. Share satisfying rule A 2^-5.9996; per set between 0.931 and 1.075 times 2^-6 (one binomial sd 0.0166; H3 needs below 1.1429); chi-square 8,358.7 on 8,192. Batches entering stage 2: 0.10383 overall, at most 0.1112 per set (budget 0.125). The three most extreme sets give 0.9994, 0.9998 and 1.0018 on 64 fresh samples each. 33,688 lanes compared with the real messages, 0 wrong. Batches are sampled, not enumerated.
findings.fix: Main session reruns "python -B review\judge_h3.py 8192 15 5 0" and adds the result to H3's extrapolation and Section 10 as a helper agent's computation. Replace "four runs cannot exclude" by what 8,192 sets with none above the budget allow (at most about 3.7e-4 of the seed sets at 95%, for the sampled share).

findings.what: As the judge I would mark H1 "plausible" (partly supported), unchanged from the pkg4 draft: stated model, counted rate, margin 3.57, candid limits; against it about 70 bits of extrapolation (tested near 2^-32, used at 2^-103), constants and class chosen by the count, independence assumed, no slack on the probability side. The new part holds up: Lemma A is correct (I rederived S, ALL, V by hand), the dropping of 40 outcomes is conservative and three solvers agree, and the printed violating solution checks (R = 0, h1 = d87fa4af, bits 23 and 24 both 0, beta f8342852). I found no concrete flaw that would justify "refuted".
findings.fix: None beyond the findings above. The owner should know that the support for rule A is still entirely participant computation.

findings.what: I would mark H2 "plausible", well supported: Lemma N is exact (rechecked), the measured rate 1,521 in 2^40 is 2^-29.43, the eight shared-seed runs show no spread (3.6 on 7), four more runs give 1,390, and the budget is 2^13.4 above the mean. All figures equal their files. The evidence is participant-produced, as for H2 of the filed packages.

I would mark H3 "plausible": the statement is exact about what it bounds (batches entering are at most trials satisfying rule A), the time bound does not depend on it, and the evidence is relevant (2^-6 for a uniform word; four runs each within 1.3e-5; my 8,192-set check). The weak points are a margin of only 1.143 and evidence that is all participant-produced. I verified in night_cheaper_classB3.cu l.134 and l.157 that the runs use shared seed words, X12 < 2^8 and exactly rule A. Lanes of one batch are slightly positively correlated (0.10383 of batches enter against 0.10438 for independent lanes), which is the favourable direction.
findings.fix: None required. Raising the budget to 5/32 at the same claim would use up the 3.8% charge margin; I do not recommend it.

findings.what: The judge's scale is established / plausible / unsupported / refuted; "unsupported" means no relevant evidence at all. The experiments role is told to note the absence of organizer-run evidence and never to trust participant reports. pkg5 adds a third declared heuristic and so one more place where a single "unsupported" leaves no score, for a gain of 1.0 bit over pkg4. H3 has the same kind of support as H2 of the filed packages, with far less margin.
findings.fix: Owner's decision between pkg4 (100.4, two heuristics) and pkg5 (99.4, three). If possible, read what the roles wrote on H2 of the filed packages first.
